Q386991: City in Coahuila, the main city of the Comarca Lagunera with Gómez Palacio and Lerdo.
One of Mexico's youngest big cities, grown since the 1880s with railways and cotton.
Its Cristo de las Noas statue is one of the largest in Latin America.
Q24826: Port city on the Mersey estuary in northwest England.
Grew rich from the Atlantic trade, including the slave trade, and as an emigration port to America.
Home of the first inter-city railway (to Manchester, 1830) and the Beatles.
Famous for its waterfront (Royal Albert Dock) and the football clubs Liverpool and Everton.
Q73045: City in central Shanxi, merged with Taiyuan into one urban area.
Includes Pingyao, a perfectly preserved Ming-dynasty walled town (World Heritage Site).
Home of the grand merchant family compounds, like the Qiao Family Compound.
Shanxi merchants from here founded China's first banks (piaohao).
Q168376: Capital of Espírito Santo, mostly on an island in a bay.
Founded in 1551, one of the oldest cities in Brazil.
A major port for iron ore exports from Minas Gerais.
Known for the Convento da Penha in neighbouring Vila Velha and for moqueca capixaba (fish stew in clay pots).
Q23337: Capital of Utah, near the Great Salt Lake.
Founded in 1847 by Mormon pioneers led by Brigham Young; headquarters of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints.
Temple Square with the Salt Lake Temple is the city's centre.
Hosted the 2002 Winter Olympics and will again in 2034.
Q221436: Capital of Borno State in northeastern Nigeria, near Lake Chad.
Founded in 1907 as a British military outpost.
Birthplace of the Boko Haram insurgency in 2009.
Seat of the Shehu of Borno, heir of the old Kanem-Bornu empire.
Q199528: Capital of Uttarakhand, in the Doon Valley at the foot of the Himalayas.
Home of the Indian Military Academy and the Forest Research Institute.
Known for elite boarding schools like the Doon School.
Gateway to the hill station Mussoorie and to Rishikesh.
Q23438: Capital of Turkmenistan, between the Karakum Desert and the Kopet Dag mountains.
Destroyed by the 1948 earthquake and rebuilt; holds the Guinness record for the most white-marble buildings.
Has many gold statues and monumental projects of its presidents.
Near the ancient Parthian city of Nisa.
Q486149: Near the Huangguoshu Waterfall, one of the largest waterfalls in China.
Known for the Longgong (Dragon Palace) caves and the Tunpu villages of Ming garrison descendants.
Famous for batik made by the Miao and Buyi people.
Q18383: Capital of Rhode Island, at the head of Narragansett Bay.
Founded in 1636 by Roger Williams as a haven of religious freedom.
An early centre of the American Industrial Revolution (Slater Mill nearby).
Home of Brown University and the Rhode Island School of Design; known for WaterFire on its rivers.
Q199440: Capital of Baja California, on the border opposite Calexico, California.
Has one of Mexico's largest Chinese communities and its own Chinese food style; La Chinesca is its Chinatown.
One of the hottest cities in Mexico; a manufacturing (maquiladora) centre.
Q533157: Gansu's second-largest city, on the upper Wei River.
The Maijishan Grottoes, with thousands of Buddhist sculptures on a cliff, are part of a Silk Road World Heritage Site.
Believed to be the birthplace of Fuxi, a legendary ancestor of the Chinese; the Fuxi Temple is here.
Known for its apples and peaches.
Q598985: City in Bihar on the north bank of the Ganges, in the Mithila region.
Kanwar Lake nearby is a Ramsar wetland and large bird sanctuary.
Has a big oil refinery (Barauni) and fertiliser and power plants.
Q8156: Capital of Lampung province at the southern tip of Sumatra.
The main gateway between Sumatra and Java via the Bakauheni ferry across the Sunda Strait.
Hit by the tsunami from the 1883 Krakatoa eruption; the volcano lies offshore.
A centre of coffee, pepper and tapioca trade.
Q4307501: The urban district of Krasnodar in southern Russia, on the Kuban River.
Founded in 1793 by Catherine the Great as Yekaterinodar, a base for the Black Sea Cossacks.
Centre of Russia's richest farming region.
Home of FC Krasnodar and its stadium.
Q485496: Kazakhstan's third city, in the south near Uzbekistan.
An old Silk Road town on the caravan route between Tashkent and China.
The ancient city Sayram, with Islamic shrines, is nearby.
Has a big oil refinery and is a railway junction.
Q41621: Israel's third city and main port, on the slopes of Mount Carmel.
The Bahá'í World Centre and its terraced gardens are a World Heritage Site.
Home of the Technion, Israel's oldest university.
A mixed city of Jews and Arabs; has the Carmelit, one of the world's smallest metro systems.
Q1658159: City and local government area in Lagos State, northeast of Lagos.
Lies on the Lagos Lagoon next to Ogun State.
One of the fastest-growing parts of the Lagos region.
Q79952: Aguascalientes, capital of the state of the same name in central Mexico; the name means 'hot waters'.
Hosts the Feria de San Marcos, one of Mexico's biggest fairs, every spring.
Its colonial centre is built over tunnels whose purpose is still unclear.
A car-making hub with large Nissan plants.
Q404362: Industrial city in northern Henan, north of the Yellow River.
Known for its manufacturing of batteries and electric motors.
Muye, where the Zhou defeated the Shang around 1046 BC, is in the area.
Baiquan springs and the Taihang Mountains are nearby.
Q33377: City in Indian Punjab on the Grand Trunk Road.
India's biggest sports goods manufacturing centre.
Many emigrants to the UK and Canada come from the area; called the 'NRI hub'.
Hosts the Harballabh music festival, one of the oldest in India.
Q131818: Algeria's second city, on the Mediterranean in the northwest.
Founded in 902 by Andalusian traders; ruled by Spain for most of 1509–1792.
Setting of Albert Camus's novel 'The Plague'; the Santa Cruz fort overlooks the city.
Q5087: City in northern West Bengal at the foot of the Himalayas.
Called the 'Gateway of Northeast India' because it lies on the narrow Siliguri Corridor ('Chicken's Neck').
Close to the borders of Nepal, Bhutan and Bangladesh.
Hub for tea trade and the start of the Darjeeling Himalayan toy train.
Q126995: City in Shaanxi east of Xi'an, south of the Wei River.
Mount Hua, one of China's five sacred mountains, known for its dangerous plank walk, is in the prefecture.
Hometown of the historian Sima Qian (Hancheng).
Q16563: City in Tennessee on the Mississippi River.
Birthplace of blues on Beale Street and of rock 'n' roll; Elvis Presley's Graceland is here.
Martin Luther King Jr. was assassinated at the Lorraine Motel in 1968, now a civil rights museum.
Headquarters of FedEx, whose hub makes Memphis airport one of the busiest cargo airports.
Q277966: Capital of Kasaï Province in DR Congo, near the Angolan border.
Founded as a diamond-mining town by the Forminière company in the early 20th century.
Lies where the Tshikapa and Kasai rivers meet.
Q524250: Coastal county-level city in Zhejiang under Taizhou.
The first place on the Chinese mainland to see sunrise in the new millennium (Shitang).
Known for pumps and shoe manufacturing; often hit by typhoons.
Q216077: City in Jiangxi on the Yangtze, near Poyang Lake.
Mount Lu (Lushan), with its villas and a World Heritage landscape, is next to the city.
One of the four great rice markets of old China; Bai Juyi wrote 'Song of the Pipa' here.
Q7253: Capital of West Sumatra on the Indian Ocean.
Centre of the Minangkabau people, known for their matrilineal culture and horn-shaped roofs.
Gave its name to Padang food, served across Indonesia (e.g. rendang).
Q898: Siberian city on the Irtysh River, a stop on the Trans-Siberian Railway.
Dostoevsky was imprisoned here in a labour camp (1850–54).
Capital of Admiral Kolchak's anti-Bolshevik White government in 1918–1920, which held the imperial gold reserve.
Q36399: City in central Vietnam on the Perfume River.
The imperial capital of the Nguyễn dynasty (1802–1945).
Its Citadel, Forbidden Purple City and royal tombs are a World Heritage Site.
Heavily damaged in the 1968 Battle of Huế; known for its spicy cuisine like bún bò Huế.
Q919: City in Siberia on the Yenisei River.
Anton Chekhov called it the most beautiful city in Siberia; it appears on the 10-ruble note.
One of the largest aluminium producers in Russia.
Near the Stolby nature reserve with its rock pillars.
Q136456637: Biên Hòa, in Đồng Nai province, is an industrial city just northeast of Ho Chi Minh City.
Founded in the 17th century by Chinese and Vietnamese settlers on the Đồng Nai River.
Site of a large US air base during the Vietnam War.
A centre of industrial parks and ceramics.
Q894: City on the Volga in Russia; called Kuybyshev from 1935 to 1991.
In WWII it was the planned backup capital: Stalin had a deep bunker built here.
A centre of the space industry: it built the rockets for Gagarin's flight.
Famous for its long Volga embankment and Zhiguli beer.
Q911: Capital of Bashkortostan, at the confluence of the Belaya and Ufa rivers.
Founded in 1574 as a fortress under Ivan the Terrible.
A centre of oil refining and chemicals.
The statue of Salawat Yulayev, Bashkir national hero, overlooks the river.
Q68862: City in southwestern Fujian; the name means 'dragon rock'.
Its Hakka tulou earthen houses in Yongding are part of a World Heritage Site.
Gutian, where the Red Army held a famous 1929 conference, is in the area.
Q75230: Coastal city in Liaoning on Liaodong Bay.
Built around the Liaohe oil field.
Famous for its Red Beach, where a seaweed turns the wetlands bright red in autumn.
Known for rice and river crabs.
Q360235: Industrial city in Anhui on the Yangtze, next to Nanjing; the name means 'saddle mountain'.
Called 'Steel City' for the Masteel works.
Also called 'Poetry City': the poet Li Bai died nearby at Caishiji, where legend says he drowned trying to embrace the moon's reflection.
Q43421: Capital of Virginia, on the James River.
Patrick Henry gave his 'Give me liberty or give me death!' speech here in 1775.
Capital of the Confederate States during the Civil War.
Its Monument Avenue statues of Confederate leaders were removed in 2020–21.
Q37400: Capital of Myanmar since 2005, a planned city built in secret by the military government.
Famous for very wide, mostly empty highways (up to 20 lanes).
Has the Uppatasanti Pagoda, a near-copy of Yangon's Shwedagon Pagoda.
Q363391: City in northeastern Jiangxi on the Fu River (not to be confused with Fuzhou in Fujian).
Hometown of the playwright Tang Xianzu ('The Peony Pavilion') and the reformer Wang Anshi.
Called a 'land of talents' for its many scholars.
Q243293: Twin city on Ghana's west coast, capital of the Western Region.
Grew from 17th-century Dutch and English forts.
Takoradi harbour (1928) was Ghana's first deep-water port.
Centre of Ghana's offshore oil industry since 2010 ('Oil City').
Q363326: City in western Jiangxi; the name means 'pleasant spring'.
Home of Mount Mingyue and hot springs.
A big lithium-mining area, important for batteries.
Tradition links it to the Zen monastic rules of Baizhang.
Q18459: Fast-growing city in Gyeonggi Province, south of Seoul.
Home of Everland, South Korea's largest theme park, and the Korean Folk Village.
Location of a huge new Samsung and SK Hynix semiconductor cluster.
Q459360: Capital of Cabinda, an exclave of Angola separated by a strip of DR Congo.
Offshore oil from Cabinda provides much of Angola's oil.
A separatist movement claims independence for Cabinda.
Q217568: The largest urban area of The Gambia, near the capital Banjul.
Grew because Banjul, on a small island, had no room to expand.
Its market is the largest in the country.
Named after its founder, Sayerr Jobe.
Q312723: The largest city of the Nile Delta's Gharbia Governorate.
Centre of Egypt's textile industry; the Misr Spinning and Weaving Company is one of the largest in Africa.
Its workers' strike in 2008 was a forerunner of the 2011 revolution.
Q204245: Capital of Morelos, south of Mexico City.
Called the 'City of Eternal Spring'; a weekend retreat for Mexico City residents.
Hernán Cortés built a palace here; Emperor Maximilian had a summer house.
Has many Spanish-language schools for foreigners.
Q255455: Winter capital of Indian-administered Jammu and Kashmir, on the Tawi River.
Called the 'City of Temples', e.g. the Raghunath Temple.
Base for pilgrims to the Vaishno Devi shrine.
Former seat of the Dogra maharajas.
Q131694: Ancient port on the Gulf of Aden near the entrance to the Red Sea.
Built partly inside the crater of an extinct volcano (Crater district).
A British colony from 1839 to 1967 and a key coaling station on the route to India.
Capital of South Yemen until 1990; seat of Yemen's recognised government since 2015.
Q61302: Capital of the Mexican state of Chihuahua.
Pancho Villa lived here; his house is now a museum of the Revolution.
Briefly capital of Mexico in 1864 under Benito Juárez during the French intervention.
Miguel Hidalgo, father of Mexican independence, was executed here in 1811.
Q365: Germany's fourth-largest city, on the Rhine.
Founded by the Romans as Colonia; its Gothic cathedral took over 600 years to complete (1248–1880).
Famous for its carnival, Kölsch beer and Eau de Cologne perfume.
About 90% destroyed in WWII; the cathedral survived.
Q173310: City in northern Iraq with a mix of Kurds, Turkmens and Arabs.
Built around an ancient citadel; the ancient city Arrapha.
Sits on one of the world's largest oil fields; oil was struck at Baba Gurgur in 1927.
Its status is disputed between Baghdad and the Kurdistan Region.
Q3642: Capital of Eritrea, at 2,325 m on the highland plateau.
Built up by the Italians as the capital of their colony; called 'Africa's Little Rome'.
Its modernist and Art Deco architecture (e.g. the Fiat Tagliero garage) is a World Heritage Site.
Known for its café culture with espresso and cappuccino.
Q1856565: The metropolitan municipality around Gqeberha (Port Elizabeth) on Algoa Bay, Eastern Cape.
Includes the towns of Kariega (Uitenhage) and Despatch.
Named after Nelson Mandela; a centre of South Africa's car industry.
Q657072: Holy city of the Mouride Sufi brotherhood in central Senegal.
Founded in 1887 by Sheikh Ahmadou Bamba; his tomb is beside the Great Mosque (1963), one of Africa's largest.
The yearly Grand Magal pilgrimage draws millions.
Run by the brotherhood with special status: alcohol and tobacco are banned.
Q416748: City in southern Hunan, bordering Guangdong.
Dongjiang Lake, with its morning mists, is a famous sight.
A big mining area for non-ferrous metals ('Silver Capital of China').
Mount Suxian is linked to Taoist legends.
Q41278: South Korea's industrial powerhouse, on the southeast coast.
Has the world's largest car factory (Hyundai) and one of the largest shipyards (Hyundai Heavy Industries).
The Bangudae petroglyphs show prehistoric whale hunting.
The richest Korean region per person.
Q1020659: District of Ankara Province, about 27 km west of the city centre.
Home of Ankara's biggest organised industrial zone.
Grew rapidly as a working-class suburb of the capital.
Q851576: Capital of South Darfur in western Sudan.
The name means 'place of chatting' in the Daju language.
A trading centre and railway terminus for western Sudan; deeply affected by the Darfur conflicts.
